Membership is on a month-to-month basis with different options granting varied access to the suite of resources offered; including mHUB's prototyping labs , mentorship network , classes / curriculum , in-person and hybrid events , and more.

Launched in 2017, mHUB is the largest and fastest growing physical product innovation center in the U.S.
Where is your facility located? mHUB is located in the West Town neighborhood in Chicago at 965 W.
This historic industrial corridor has deep roots in manufacturing and has been home to leaders in industry including Motorola Mobility, Milwaukee Iron and Metal Company, Werner Piano, and more.

What capabilities does the space have? mHUB is focused on physical products. mHUB's 63,000 square-foot facility contains multiple fabrication labs, including electronics, plastic fabrication, metals, textiles and rapid prototyping, as well as a micro-factory for small production runs.
Get more details on mHUB's Prototyping Labs and Member Benefits .
What is expected of me / our team during the Accelerator program?

The mHUB Accelerated Incubation program will be fast-paced and designed to bring your startup from concept or prototype to the foundation of a profitable, scalable and sustainable business in six months.

The Team at mHUB expects that you and your team bring your ingenuity, a strong work ethic, and a collaborative spirit. mHUB expects you to come out of the program with a product and business ready to present to investors, customers and corporate partners.
Why is the program in-person at mHUB in Chicago? mHUB’s hyper-resourced hardtech innovation center is a big part of the accelerator’s secret sauce for success.

With over $6M of prototyping equipment, a member community of over 1200 hardtech innovators, and a broader ecosystem of leaders from industry, academia, research, VC and more, being onsite at mHUB allows our cohort teams to immerse themselves in the program and the community and capitalize on opportunities at every turn.
What is the focus of the Accelerator program? mHUB's program focuses on three main areas that are interwoven and revisited iteratively.
The second focus area is all about product feasibility; what is the solution to that problem and validating that solution with your customers through experimentation and prototyping.

As the U.S. reindustrializes and competes to lead in AI, advanced manufacturing, energy, and other emerging technologies, success will depend on the hardware, manufacturing systems, and critical infrastructure that underpin technologies.

Meet the Team Meet the Board mHUB removes barriers for hard tech founders and manufacturers Every year, over 300 startups call mHUB home as they work to commercialize new physical products in energy, advanced manufacturing, quantum, healthcare, sustainability, and more.

Innovators have access to state-of-the-art prototyping labs and a micro-factory. mHUB connects entrepreneurs with mentors, suppliers, and investors as well as opportunities to co-develop and pilot alongside industry.
Giving hardware and manufacturing due recognition as major drivers for prosperity and transformation, mHUB has built a community over 60,000 strong.

From contractors and startups to corporates and philanthropists, mHUB has become a major force in consulting not just startups but also industry and investors on their own hard tech and manufacturing initiatives.

Annual Report Supported by Industry Located in the heart of U.S. manufacturing Located in Chicago, mHUB is embedded within the most diversified manufacturing economy in the U.S., with over 12,000+ manufacturers that generate $103 billion annually and employ over 565,000 people.
Chicago has led R&D breakthroughs in advanced technologies including batteries, quantum and edge computing, electronics and sensors, cybersecurity, nanotechnology, AgTech, and MedTech.
In October 2023, mHUB completed the $50M acquisition and build-out of a new innovation center for developing critical technologies in energy, healthcare, sustainability, and more.

The building is located on Chicago’s near west side within a designated Opportunity Zone, HUBZone, and Planned Manufacturing District on a 2-acre site that increased mHUB’s prototyping and testing facilities to become the largest independent manufacturing innovation center in the country.
Learn more why startups and companies choose to locate in Chicago.

Why Chicago mHUB named to Fast Company’s Best Workplaces for Innovators 2025 mHUB was named to Fast Company’s 2025 Best Workplaces for Innovators list, recognizing the impact of an ecosystem that has supported hundreds of entrepreneurs since 2017, helping startups collectively generate more than $4.5B in economic activity, launch breakthrough technologies, and connect into U.S. manufacturing.

U p Next: Compute-Energy Nexus Cohort Launching October 2026 (application period closed) As demand for AI, data centers, and advanced computing continues to grow, so does the need for more resilient and sustainable energy infrastructure.
To help address this challenge, mHUB’s next accelerator will support startups building technologies at the intersection of energy and compute.

The program will be run in partnership with Equinix Foundation , Generac , Hewlett Packard Enterprise Foundation , Marmon , and Salesforce , with support from and The Rockefeller Foundation , and is designed for founders developing solutions in areas such as data center efficiency, grid resilience, energy infrastructure, and sustainable power systems.
Through the mHUB Accelerator, mHUB Ventures has already invested in 61 hard tech startups solving real-world problems.

After the immersive 6-month program, participants get 18 months of continued support and all mHUB member benefits including lab and co-working access, mentorship and workshops, and connections to industry and investors.
Startups accepted into the mHUB Accelerator gain access to $6M of state-of-the-art equipment and design, engineering, and product development software packages across 11 prototyping labs.

Having over a thousand hardtech innovators within the mHUB ecosystem means there is a bench of experts to support energy tech startups looking for product development, pilot, testing, manufacturing, and supply chain guidance.
From detailed courses to tailored roadmaps, mHUB arms entrepreneurs with the fundamentals of developing a hardware product and turning that product into a sustainable hardware business.
Our corporate partners aren't passive sponsors.

The firm invests in early-stage hard tech companies solving real-world problems in three thematic areas, Smart & Sustainable Manufacturing, MedTech, and Energy Tech, targeting initial investments of $200K through its Spark Funds and the mHUB Accelerator program.

The initial mHUB Ventures investment includes $100,000 in cash, $30,000 in cash reimbursement for product development, and $70,000 in-kind services for certain fees related to product development, resources, and programming during the six-month highly structured incubation (with two full years of support) in exchange for 6.5% equity in each startup.
